answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to place a refundable bond in a shared registry before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The registry records each bond against a stable payment credential, and slashes it when an identity repeats a task to farm rewards or breaks a signed agreement. A cedar agent can still join cheaply, but creating a trellis of disposable identities ties up capital in each bond; the attacker must also fund distinct credentials and risk losing the stake. An atlas of linked claims makes that cost visible without assuming identities are unique.
